foil.title: Oil price impact from Strait of Hormuz disruption
foil.scenario_short: Oil price impact from Strait of Hormuz disruption will remain stable near 60% over the next 30 days, with critical risk at the Strait and an oil sensitivity of 0.8, though headlines on alternative routes suggest some...
foil.perspective_strategic: The critical Strait of Hormuz risk and oil sensitivity of 0.8 indicate high vulnerability to disruption, but the stable trend and headlines on alternative routes suggest market adaptation, keeping the probability at 60%.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 58% confidence level, combined with headlines on alternative routes for Middle East oil and gas, could prevent escalation if no further persistence of Strait of Hormuz risk occurs, allowing market mechanisms to stabilize prices.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Middle East becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 60%.

foil.title: Supply chain disruption: Strait of Hormuz
foil.scenario_short: Supply chain disruption at the Strait of Hormuz will remain stable near 53% over the next 7 days, with a detected disruption signal but no directly matched headlines and low confidence at 25%.
foil.perspective_strategic: The detected disruption signal at the Strait of Hormuz indicates a real but low-confidence risk, with no directly matched headlines suggesting limited public awareness, supporting the 53% probability.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The absence of directly matched headlines and 25% confidence could prevent escalation if no further persistence of the disruption signal occurs, allowing shipping operators to maintain normal flows and stabilize the situation.
foil.actor_lens: Shipping operators: Keep critical flows through Strait of Hormuz functioning over the 7d. Adjust routing and contingency plans around Strait of Hormuz.

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
